committees.name: Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions Committee

dimensions.assessment: Affects individuals living with traumatic brain injuries, state health agencies, American Indian consortiums, protection and advocacy agencies, and high-risk populations such as public safety officers and survivors of domestic violence.
dimensions.evidence: services and support for individuals living with traumatic brain injuries, and ACL grants for protection and advocacy agencies supporting individuals with traumatic brain injuries.

dimensions.assessment: Moderate effects through continued and expanded grant funding, enhanced data collection, public awareness campaigns, and mandatory federal reporting on long-term conditions.
dimensions.evidence: reauthorizes and expands Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) programs relating to traumatic brain injuries.

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes specific federal appropriations of $9,250,000 annually for CDC surveillance and registries and $13,118,000 annually for state programs relating to traumatic brain injury for fiscal years 2026 through 2030.
dimensions.evidence: appropriated $9,250,000 for each of fiscal years 2026 through 2030... $13,118,000 for each of fiscal years 2026 through 2030.

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Public Health Service Act to rename and expand existing surveillance, registry, and grant programs, add maintenance of effort and matching waiver rules, and mandate specific federal studies.
dimensions.evidence: The Bill Pascrell, Jr., National Program for Traumatic Brain Injury Surveillance and Registries

dimensions.assessment: Provides a 5-year reauthorization spanning fiscal years 2026 through 2030 alongside ongoing reporting and study requirements.
dimensions.evidence: for each of fiscal years 2026 through 2030

missing_information: The exact number of individuals who will receive direct services through the reauthorized state grants.
importance_detail.rationale: H.R. 1493 reauthorizes and expands federal traumatic brain injury programs at the CDC and ACL through fiscal year 2030, sets specific funding authorizations, and mandates federal studies and reports on high-risk populations and long-term symptoms.
